QF.id: SIA Social Impact Assessment and Assessors_40

question.text: During data analysis, to avoid over-claiming impact, the SIA review process should ask which of the following questions?

answer.text: What was the situation before and what would have happened in the absence of this project/program? How much did the project contribute to the changes? How much unintended impact (positive and negative) resulted?
What is the SE's CSR commitment next year?
What is the SE's return on equity benchmarked to peers?
What is the anticipated IPO valuation of the FPE once SSE-listed?

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 5.11.4 Data Analysis sub-section specifies three stakeholder-feedback questions to 'help assess the impact, validate and establish a check and avoid overclaiming': (1) What was the situation before, and what would have happened absent the project (counterfactual/deadweight)? (2) How much did the project contribute (attribution/contribution)? (3) What unintended positive or negative impacts resulted? The Trap: B (CSR commitment), C (ROE), and D (IPO valuation) are corporate-finance or CSR-planning questions, unrelated to impact over-claim analysis. Cross-Exam Context: Counterfactual / attribution / unintended consequences are core impact-economics concepts — unique to XXIII; not tested in prior exams. Assessor's Pro-Tip: For every key impact claim in the AIR, write a one-line test against each of the three questions in Section 5.11.4 — if you cannot answer any one, the claim probably over-states impact.
